 Zverev Stays Perfect in Turin, Overcomes Fils and Ankle Scare
 World No.1 Alexander Zverev overcame an injury scare and remained undefeated at the ATP Finals on Thursday. 
 Chris Oddo November 19, 2026 3 minute read 
 Share X Facebook WhatsApp Email Copy link More… 
 Listen to this article 
 1× 
 ✕ 
 Leading into these ATP Finals, the chatter among media and critics of Alexander Zverev was that he had an impoverished record against the Top 10. The critics weren’t wrong – the German entered the tournament with a 3-9 record against the Top 10, and was gaining mention for having played one of the most bizarre seasons ever turned in by a year-end No. 1 – but a week later, the argument doesn’t hold as much water.
 Zverev notched his third consecutive Top 10 win on Thursday in Turin, taking out Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6), as he moved through the John McEnroe Group undefeated to take his spot in the semifinals.
 Zverev, who suffered an ankle issue in the waning moments of the final set, had to scrap to get through in two. He had signaled for the trainer and looked to be in big trouble after squandering a 6-1 lead in the second-set breaker before finally finishing off Fils.
 A sigh of relief for Zverev, who improved to 3-0 in group play and 6-0 in sets at the ATP Finals. He didn’t drop serve in any of his three wins.
 Unbroken. Unbeaten. 🫡 @AlexZverev completes a clean sweep of the John McEnroe group en route to the #NittoATPFinals semis pic.twitter.com/90UqzgBLcb 
— Tennis TV (@TennisTV) November 19, 2026 
 “Unfortunately, I started feeling my ankle again,” Zverev told ATP Media on court after the match.
 “I’ll probably feel my ankle sometimes until the end of my career. It’s unfortunately, the injury that I had, it’s quite big. I’m going to do everything I can to be pain-free on Saturday, but this is something that I have to live with nowadays.”
 The German is one of just seven players to have reached the semifinals at the ATP Finals without dropping a set since 2000, and one of four to have achieved the feat twice (also 2024). The others are Novak Djokovic (3), Roger Federer (3), Jannik Sinner (2), Daniil Medvedev (1), Nikolay Davydenko (1) and Andy Roddick (1).
 The 29-year-old, who scored wins against No. 10-ranked Rafael Jodar, No. 4-ranked Ben Shelton and No. 7-ranked Fils this week, still has plenty to prove. He’ll join a semifinal quartet that also includes Carlos Alcaraz, the man who defeated him in the Australian Open semifinals in January, as he bids to run the table and claim his third ATP Finals title (also 2018 and 2021).
 Truth be told, no matter what happens, Zverev has far outperformed expectations in 2026. He shed the best-player-to-never-win-a-Slam moniker by winning the Roland Garros title and backed that up with a Wimbledon final and his second major title, won at the US Open in September.
 He leads the tour with 68 wins and has never played more convincingly under pressure, in the biggest moments and on the biggest stages. That said, Zverev’s combined 0-6 record against Alcaraz (0-1) and Sinner (0-5) in 2026 makes him a world No. 1 who plays like a world No. 3.
 In Shadow of Sinner, Zverev Asserts Authority as World No. 1 
 It’s a dirty job, but someone has to do it.
 This weekend, Zverev will look to prove that he can go through Alcaraz – whom he could face in the semis or final in Turin – to win a prestigious title.
 Against Fils on Thursday, he didn’t expend too much energy, breaking the 22-year-old Frenchman’s serve in the seventh game of the match and never facing a break point as he dropped just five points on serve in the set.
 “I thought the first two matches were very, very high level,” said the world No. 1. “Today I thought I played a little bit worse from the baseline. I’m very happy to have won all three matches against three very difficult opponents.
 “Arthur, for me personally, is a very difficult opponent as well because of how much power he has – I’m happy to be through in straight sets.”
